title: Microsoft Teams: external presenters in event group chat
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's updated notice, including the late March to mid-April 2027 rollout and conditional access to earlier messages. The documented controls and licensing statements are supported; no blocking corrections were found.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing
claims.claim: Microsoft plans external presenter support for Teams event group chat.
claims.quote: Event group chat, the private chat for organizers, co-organizers, and presenters in an event or structured meeting, will support external presenters.

claims.claim: Event group chat is private chat for organisers, co-organisers and presenters in an event or structured meeting.
claims.quote: Event group chat, the private chat for organizers, co-organizers, and presenters in an event or structured meeting

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope: Who
claims.claim: Presenters outside the hosting tenant will be able to participate in event group chat.
claims.quote: This change enables presenters who are outside the tenant hosting the meeting or event to participate in the event group chat.

claims.where: What's changing: existing chat
claims.claim: For events optimised for large audiences, event group chat is available before, during and after the event.
claims.quote: The event group chat is available before, during, and after an event, and is a separate experience from the chat with attendees.

3. In the list of policies, select the Org-wide default settings.
4. Adjust the settings as you need.

claims.where: Governance controls: PowerShell domain parameters

claims.quote: Domain objects (created by using the New-CsEdgeAllowList cmdlet or the New-CsEdgeAllowAllKnownDomains cmdlet) that represent the domains that users are allowed to communicate with.

claims.where: Governance controls: PowerShell domain parameters

claims.quote: Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -BlockedDomains @{Replace=$x}

claims.where: Governance controls: separate PowerShell operations
claims.claim: Domain lists can be set in their own cmdlet calls separately from the federation-enabling call.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -BlockedDomains $Null

Example 5 shows how you can remove all the domains assigned to the blocked domains list for the current tenant
